## Summary

Fixed `parse_metadata_block` in `registry/model.py:251` — it previously located the identity block by naively splitting on the first `METADATA_BEGIN`/`METADATA_END` it found, while the writer (`upsert_metadata_block`, via `_metadata_bounds`) locates the innermost well-formed BEGIN/END pair. A task description quoting an unfinished example block (before or after the real block) could hijack the reader, inventing fields like `parent` or `depends-on` from the quoted text, or corrupting identity resolution.

The fix makes `parse_metadata_block` call the same `_metadata_bounds` helper the writer already uses, so both agree on which block is authoritative. When no complete, well-formed pair exists, it now returns `{}` (no metadata), matching the writer's own fallback behavior.

Verified:
- Leading and trailing unfinished/quoted example blocks are ignored; the real block is still parsed correctly.
- A body with only an unfinished example reads as no metadata.
- Repeated `evidence`/`reproduction`/`proposed-fix` entries and comma-containing prose still round-trip.
- `upsert_metadata_block` still updates only the real block in place, preserving surrounding human text and the quoted example verbatim.
- Both consumers (`registry/providers/local.py`, `registry/providers/github.py`) go through this shared function, so no other changes were needed.

Added regression coverage in `tests/test_metadata_block.py` (stdlib `unittest`, no new deps) — all 7 tests pass. No files were pushed or committed, per your instructions.
